claims.text: Chemical short-range order typically suppresses lattice thermal conductivity in concentrated refractory high-entropy alloys.
SRO suppresses lattice heat transport by enhancing phonon scattering rather than through an ordering-dominated transport regime.
SRO creates local chemical-potential fluctuations that strongly scatter mid-to-high-frequency phonons.
SRO can reduce the phonon mean free path below an interatomic-spacing limit characteristic of disordered alloys.
Nominally disordered concentrated RHEAs have low lattice thermal conductivity because of mass-disorder and lattice-distortion scattering.
The Mo-Nb-Ta-V-W system has a propensity to form chemical short-range order.
Controlled thermal annealing can induce or enhance SRO without producing a long-range superlattice.
Radiation-assisted treatment can induce or enhance SRO in concentrated RHEAs.
The proposed regime applies over 300-1500 K in alloys having atomic-mass variance greater than 15%.
Relevant annealing temperatures lie above the onset of ordering and below the melting point.
B2-like or L12-like local motifs generate spatially varying force constants and mass distributions.
Spatial variations associated with local ordering act as resonant or Rayleigh phonon-scattering centers.
SRO creates potential-energy landscapes with spatial frequencies that match phonon wavelengths and thereby produce resonant scattering.
SRO reduces phonon mean free paths more strongly than random mass fluctuations in a fully disordered state.
The SRO-induced suppression is strongest at intermediate temperatures before phonon-phonon Umklapp scattering becomes dominant.
Lattice thermal conductivity decreases monotonically as the degree of SRO increases.
SRO may suppress lattice thermal conductivity by 10-30%.
Disordered RHEAs typically have room-temperature lattice thermal conductivity of 5-15 W/m·K.
The proposed suppression is limited to single-phase RHEAs without precipitation, phase separation, or long-range ordering.
An increase in lattice thermal conductivity in the SRO-rich sample relative to an otherwise identical disordered sample would falsify the proposed suppression hypothesis.
